body:
## Why

A repository created from the Template starts without the `priority:*` label family, and the opener lane's selection is ordered by exactly that family. Its own round records say so: "selected the oldest unlinked **priority-normal** supported implementation issue ... after mandatory priority ordering". An issue with no priority label can therefore never be the oldest priority-normal candidate, so a whole repository can sit in the fleet, be listed in `SUPPORTED_REPOS`, appear in the liveness guard's candidate set, and still never be selected.

Measured on 2026-09-13. Three repositories created on 2026-09-04 (`Doc-Lineage`, `Deliverable-Render`, `Manager-Mosaic`) plus `Ready` all had **no** `priority:*` labels, while every established repository has `priority:high`, `priority:normal` and `priority:low`. The labels have since been created by hand and the backlogs labelled, which is the remedy, not the fix.

The defect propagates quietly: the usual way to set up a new repository is `gh label clone` from an existing one, and `Ready`, the natural donor, is itself missing the family. Cloning from it reproduces the gap every time.

## Scope

Make the `priority:*` family part of consumer bootstrap, and make its absence detectable rather than silent.

## Non-Goals

- No change to the opener's selection policy. Ordering by priority is correct.
- No automatic labelling of existing issues by guessing their importance.
- No new label vocabulary. The three existing values are enough.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `scripts/bootstrap_consumer_settings.py`, add `priority:high`, `priority:normal` and `priority:low` with the colours and descriptions the established repositories already use.
- [ ] In `stranske/Template`, add the same three labels so a repository created from the template has them before any bootstrap runs.
- [ ] In `scripts/bootstrap_consumer_settings.py`, add a consumer health check that fails when a registered consumer lacks any label the opener's selection depends on, naming the repository and the missing labels.
- [ ] In `scripts/bootstrap_consumer_settings.py`, make the check report open implementation issue count and priority-labelled count for every registered consumer, including zeros.
- [ ] In `docs/ops/CONSUMER_REPO_MAINTENANCE.md`, document that the priority family is load-bearing for opener selection and must not be dropped when cloning labels between repositories.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Run `pytest tests/scripts/test_bootstrap_consumer_labels.py -q` and retain output in the PR body.
- [ ] The fixture test fails when `priority:normal` is removed from the bootstrap label set and passes once restored.
- [ ] The health check output shows issue count alongside priority-labelled count for every consumer, including zeros.
- [ ] A repository created from `stranske/Template` has the three labels with no further action.

## Implementation Notes

The wider lesson is worth encoding in the check rather than in prose: a repository can satisfy every registration surface in the fleet and still be unreachable by the lane that does the work. The check should therefore assert reachability, not membership.
